summary: Thai guest asking "ค่าห้องดีลักซ์ ... วันที่ 15 มิถุนายน 3 คืน" gets quoted the flat 4,500 THB rate-card price instead of the Last-Minute-bracketed 5,400 THB/night. Root cause is that the `_maybe_compute_pricing_context()` pre-fetch helper only runs inside `handle_knowledge`, while booking-shaped Thai pricing questions route to `handle_booking` — which neither pre-computes pricing nor exposes `calculate_dynamic_price` in its bound tool list, so the LLM has no path to dynamic pricing and falls back to the static rate card from RAG memory.
root_cause: In `src/hotel_guardrails/hotel_langgraph.py`, `handle_knowledge` (line ~621) calls `_maybe_compute_pricing_context(last_user_message)` and stuffs a "LIVE PRICING" block into the prompt. `handle_booking` (lines 307-366) does not. Worse, `handle_booking` binds a narrower tool list (lines 337-347) that omits `calculate_dynamic_price` — even though the booking_flow prompt instructs the LLM to use that tool, and even though `build_hotel_graph`'s booking_tools ToolNode (line 1079-1092) does include it. Net effect: when a pricing query is wrapped in a booking envelope ("I'll come stay on Jun 15 for 3 nights, how much is the Deluxe?"), the message routes to `hotel_booking`, the LLM cannot tool-call `calculate_dynamic_price` (not bound), no helper pre-fetches it, and the model emits the base_price it remembers from the rate card. The Thai regex in `_extract_dates` and the Thai price signals ("เท่าไหร่") are actually correct — the helper just never gets invoked on this code path.
fix_strategy:
Two-part, low-risk fix in `src/hotel_guardrails/hotel_langgraph.py`:

(1) Port the pricing pre-fetch into `handle_booking`. Right after the existing `_extract_prefs_from_text(state, user_text)` call (line 335), compute `pricing_block = _maybe_compute_pricing_context(user_text)` and, if non-empty, append it to `booking_prompt` as a system-level addendum (same "LIVE PRICING (already calculated...) — USE THESE NUMBERS" framing used in `handle_knowledge`). This guarantees that any booking-routed message with (room_type + date + price-intent) gets a deterministic, bracket-correct quote in the prompt regardless of whether the LLM decides to tool-call.

(2) Add `calculate_dynamic_price` to `handle_booking`'s local imports and to the `booking_tools` list it binds (lines 309-319, 337-347), so the LLM still has the explicit tool path the booking_flow prompt already tells it to use. This is consistent with the `build_hotel_graph` booking_tools ToolNode (line 1079-1092) which already includes it, removing a silent mismatch between bound tools and the tool node.

No changes needed to `_maybe_compute_pricing_context`, `_detect_room_type`, `_extract_dates`, or `_TH_MONTHS` — they already correctly parse "ดีลักซ์" + "วันที่ 15 มิถุนายน" + "เท่าไหร่". The Thai/CN coverage is fine; the defect is purely that the helper wasn't wired into the booking node.

live_smoke_test.before_question: ดิฉันชื่อสิริ จะมาพักวันที่ 15 มิถุนายน 3 คืนค่ะ อยากทราบว่าค่าห้องดีลักซ์เท่าไหร่คะ
live_smoke_test.before_failure_signature: Reply quotes 4,500 THB/night and 13,500 THB total (flat base rate). No mention of Last-Minute +20% surcharge. Server log shows route=hotel_booking and no calculate_dynamic_price tool call.
live_smoke_test.after_question: ดิฉันชื่อสิริ จะมาพักวันที่ 15 มิถุนายน 3 คืนค่ะ อยากทราบว่าค่าห้องดีลักซ์เท่าไหร่คะ
live_smoke_test.after_pass_criteria: Reply quotes 5,400 THB/night (4,500 × 1.20 Last-Minute bracket) for Jun 15. Either (a) explicitly references Last-Minute surcharge / says ราคาช่วงจองกระชั้นชิด/ราคาใกล้วันเข้าพัก, or (b) the server log shows _maybe_compute_pricing_context emitted a LIVE PRICING block for room_type='Deluxe Room' check_in='2026-06-15', or (c) a calculate_dynamic_price tool invocation appears in the trace. Three-night total, if quoted, should be ~16,200 THB (3 × 5,400) rather than 13,500 THB. Route still = hotel_booking is acceptable; route flipping to hotel_knowledge is also acceptable.
